result:
I worked this out by hand, enumerating the candidates in each length class and checking each one's binary popcount. I had no code execution, so this is error-prone; I rechecked the enumerations and most of the popcounts.

**Setup.** Non-decreasing digits forbid zeros, so every such n has digits 1–9 sorted. Since 10 ≡ 1 (mod 3), n ≡ 1 (mod 3) means the digit sum ≡ 1 (mod 3). The range 61 ≤ n ≤ 20000 contains:
- 2-digit: 66, 67, 68, 69, 77, 78, 79, 88, 89, 99 (those ≥ 61)
- 3-digit: all 165 non-decreasing numbers
- 4-digit: all 495
- 5-digit: the 495 starting with 1 (20000 is excluded since it has zeros)

**Counts.**
- 2-digit: digit sum ≡ 1 gives 67, 79, 88. Their popcounts are 3, 5, 3 (all odd), so 0 survive.
- 3-digit: 54 candidates with digit sum ≡ 1. Parity-even survivors: 136, 139, 166, 169, 178, 226, 235, 238, 277, 337, 349, 469, 556, 559, 568, 667, 679, 688, 778. That is **19**.
- 4-digit: 165 candidates. Survivors by leading digit: 1→17, 2→26, 3→6, 4→7, 5→3, 6→5, 7→0, 8→1, 9→0. That is **65**.
- 5-digit: 165 candidates (1bcde with b ≤ c ≤ d ≤ e and b+c+d+e ≡ 0 mod 3). Survivors by second digit: 1→37, 2→14, 3→7, 4→11, 5→1, 6→2, 7→2, 8→0, 9→0. That is **74**.

**Total:** 0 + 19 + 65 + 74 = 158.

ANSWER: 158
